roles.summary: Inspection rover: power systems and field tests.
roles.mission: Help communities inspect essential infrastructure without putting people in hazardous places.
roles.goal: Combine inspection hardware, field operations, risk assessment, and public-service partnerships into an affordable inspection service.
roles.outcome: Dissolved at graduation after failing to establish a sustainable funding path. The dissolution agreement returned individually authored IP to its creators and preserved their attributable work records.
accomplishments: Owned the rover power-distribution schematic and protection-component choices.
Integrated voltage and current telemetry with firmware teammates.
Led fault reproduction and regression checks after an intermittent field reset.

roles.summary: Adaptive gripper: controls, integration, and pilot delivery.
roles.mission: Recover more surplus food and get it to communities that need it.
roles.goal: Combine food logistics, safe handling, operator workflows, and adaptable automation to reduce the cost of redistributing surplus food.
roles.outcome: Secured outside funding at graduation to continue its food-recovery pilot. The multidisciplinary team carried its operating partnerships and handling-system development into the next phase.
accomplishments: Owned tactile sensing, actuation, and control integration.
Built Python tooling to test contact, release, and low-confidence conditions.
Worked with the product lead to define pilot limits and acceptance checks.

evidence.title: Inspection rover power system
evidence.summary: Designed and integrated the rover's protected power-distribution board.
evidence.contribution: Alex authored the board schematic, selected protection components, and wrote firmware hooks for voltage and current telemetry. Mechanical packaging and the rover's navigation software were teammates' work.
evidence.decision: Separated motor and compute power paths so a motor transient would not repeatedly reset the onboard computer.
evidence.result: The bench record includes schematic revisions, a fault-injection checklist, and telemetry traces showing how the protected paths behaved.
evidence.limits: This record has no independently verified runtime, deployment count, or certification result.

evidence.title: Recovering from a field power failure
evidence.summary: Investigated an intermittent reset during a rover field trial.
evidence.contribution: Alex coordinated reproduction, compared motor-current traces with reset events, and worked with Jordan Lee on cable routing and connector strain relief.
evidence.decision: Returned to controlled fault reproduction before changing the entire board. Recorded both the electrical hypothesis and the mechanical contributors.
evidence.result: The team revised protection settings and the harness, then added the failure condition to regression testing.
evidence.limits: The record demonstrates a diagnostic approach; it does not establish universal reliability.

evidence.title: Adaptive gripper sensing and control
evidence.summary: Integrated tactile sensing, actuation, and Python test tools for an adaptive gripper.
evidence.contribution: Alex owned integration and the test harness. Maya Chen contributed to tactile-feedback research; other specialists designed mechanical parts.
evidence.decision: Used explicit contact and release states, bounded actuator commands, and conservative behavior when sensor confidence dropped.
evidence.result: The record includes a state-transition review, recorded test cases for varied object shapes, and notes on fragile-object handling.
evidence.limits: This is a laboratory prototype, not a certified safety system or evidence of production-scale performance.

evidence.title: Turning the gripper into a customer pilot
evidence.summary: Translated prototype capability into a bounded pilot with an external user.
evidence.contribution: Alex worked with Product Lead Sam Rivera to define the operating envelope, acceptance checks, operator handoff, and known limitations.
evidence.decision: Narrowed the pilot to a supported object set rather than presenting broad laboratory success as general capability.
evidence.result: The pilot produced a clearer boundary between demonstrated behavior, unsupported objects, and work needed before wider delivery.
evidence.limits: No revenue, adoption, or customer satisfaction figures are claimed.

evidence.title: Canopy Systems irrigation prototype
evidence.summary: Supported sensing and actuator design for an irrigation robot prototype.
evidence.contribution: Alex helped compare sensor placement, actuator power demand, and service access with the prototype partner.
evidence.decision: Considered repair access alongside the initial parts cost rather than minimizing the bill of materials alone.
evidence.result: The tradeoff record connects electrical choices to maintenance and field use.
evidence.limits: Alex supported the prototype; this is not a claim to have designed the entire irrigation system.

evidence.title: Mentoring motor-control debugging
evidence.summary: Mentored Maya Chen and Eli Park on motor control and prototype debugging.
evidence.contribution: Alex helped the students isolate power, command, and feedback faults; asked them to explain their diagnosis before proposing a fix.
evidence.decision: Used small reproducible tests so the learners could distinguish a working patch from an understood cause.
evidence.result: The mentoring record includes a debugging checklist and teach-back prompts.
evidence.limits: The record does not claim measured learning gains or an instructional credential.

evidence.title: Personal electronics bench journal
evidence.summary: A self-directed notebook of small circuit experiments and Python measurement tools.
evidence.contribution: Alex documented setup assumptions, measurement steps, and corrections while exploring small circuits outside assigned company work.
evidence.decision: Kept unsuccessful experiments alongside working designs to preserve the reasons for changing an approach.
evidence.result: The journal shows iterative learning and a habit of recording evidence.
evidence.limits: This is an authored project outline. The actual notebook, code, and measurements have not yet been created.

evidence.title: OpenShelf venture proposal
evidence.summary: A shared-tools and repair-guidance proposal developed during the Summer Founders Program.
evidence.contribution: Mapped repair workflows, interviewed potential users, and tested the cost and service assumptions with teammates.
evidence.decision: Tested access, maintenance, and adoption assumptions before proposing a campus-backed venture.
evidence.result: Completed the program; not selected as a capstone corporation. Alex joined SafeReach and carried the customer-discovery lessons into later work.
evidence.limits: Completion of the program is distinct from capstone selection or commercial success.

evidence.title: Industry salon and technical working session
evidence.summary: Presented adaptive gripping and earned a focused session with a visiting industry leader.
evidence.contribution: Prepared the demonstration, explained failure cases, and brought specific integration questions for critique.
evidence.decision: Used the session to test the operating envelope rather than asking for a general endorsement.
evidence.result: The critique informed pilot acceptance checks and the next integration plan.
evidence.limits: Selection for a working session is not an endorsement of every capability in the profile.

evidence.title: Fault-aware power delivery for field robots
evidence.summary: Alex Morgan and collaborators · Campus working paper · 2031.
evidence.contribution: Authored the protection architecture and failure-analysis sections with contributions from the field-test team.
evidence.decision: Connected observed resets to protection settings and physical harness conditions.
evidence.result: Shared a repeatable fault-reproduction method and design lessons with the next cohort.
evidence.limits: A campus working paper, not an externally peer-reviewed journal article.

evidence.title: Low-cost tactile feedback for adaptive gripping
evidence.summary: Alex Morgan and Maya Chen · Campus working paper · 2032.
evidence.contribution: Alex authored integration and control notes; Maya developed the repeatable sensing experiment.
evidence.decision: Evaluate contact behavior and uncertainty within a bounded object set.
evidence.result: Shared a sensing and testing approach that supported the handling pilot.
evidence.limits: A campus working paper; broad performance and production safety are not established.

summary: I build useful machines and help teams make them work in the real world. My work spans protected power systems, sensing and control integration, field diagnostics, and the practical decisions that turn a prototype into a dependable service. At SafeReach and Harvest Commons, I worked with specialists in engineering, product, operations, and public service; I also mentor emerging builders and pursue ventures that make everyday capabilities more accessible.
